Q: Quaternion multiplication not working as intended A:

The error was on the line before the ret instruction in the QuatMult function. It should have been insertps xmm0, xmm1, INSERT_X_TO_W , not insertps xmm0, xmm1, INSERT_W_TO_W .

Q: JUnit: Mocking a http server A:

The Apache HttpClient library, a component of the Apache HttpComponents project, includes a specialized utility for testing known as the LocalTestServer.

See also: https://thecarlhall.wordpress.com/2010/03/25/unit-testing-with-httpclients-localtestserver/

Basic Setup

First, if you’re using Maven, you’ll need to bring in a new depedency in your pom.xml:

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.httpcomponents</groupId>
    <artifactId>httpclient</artifactId>
    <version>4.0.1</version>
    <classifier>tests</classifier>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>

Next, you’ll need to setup your unit test with the test server.

Usage

public class MyUnitTest {
   private LocalTestServer server = null;
    @Mock  HttpRequestHandler handler;
   @Before  public void setUp() {
    server = new LocalTestServer(null, null);
    server.register("/someUrl/*", handler);
    server.start();

     // report how to access the server
    String serverUrl = "http://" + server.getServiceHostName() + ":"
        + server.getServicePort();
    System.out.println("LocalTestServer available at " + serverUrl);
  }

   // do lots of testing!

   @After  public void tearDown() {
    server.stop();  
}
}

Q: Can I use unique_ptr with inherited classes? A:

Yes, by itself it can be used with caveats, the "pointee" class should have virtual destructor to free resources of derived class correctly OR you have to implement deleters were it's not possible.

The problem you stumble in is that std::unique_ptris pointer with a unique ownership. It cannot be copied, only moved because copy operations were deleted. Which affect the class Foo you add unique_ptr as a memeber varaable, in same way - it deletes copy constructor and assignment. Unique pointer is required where you have to "grab" exclusive ownership of something so it matters what you're using it for.

It's either

  1. a wrong pointer for your purpose, consider shared_ptr,

  2. you don't need a copy operation (e.g. use of PIMPL pattern which is anexample of unique_ptr use, usually prevents or discorages it) or

  3. you have to work around limitations by creating own copy procedures in class Foo.

Q: Flutter version compatibility or App Store submission guidance - Xcode 26 - Flutter 3.38 - Flutter 3.29 A:

  • Regarding Privacy Manifests, as far as I know this requirement was already introduced in 2025, and my project has already declared it. Are there any special or new requirements related to Privacy Manifests in 2026? If so, could you please share the relevant documentation or links?

  • Regarding UISceneDelegate, according to the documentation I’ve read, this is only mandatory for applications that are newly built for the latest iOS version. Since my app was originally built before iOS 26 and I am now building it with the iOS 26 SDK, it should still be fine, correct?

  • What will definitely happen if I keep using Flutter 3.29.3 and build the app with Xcode 26, given that the app is currently running smoothly?

  • If the two points above are not an issue, is there still any risk that my app could be rejected by Apple?

Thank you very much.
